Title: NASA GSFC SLR long-term 28-day estimates of C20
Date created: 28 Jan 2026
Data span: 13 Jun 1976 - 23 Nov 2025 (mid-point of solution)
Author: B.D. Loomis
Contact: bryant.d.loomis@nasa.gov, NASA GSFC, Geodesy & Geophysics Laboratory
Description:
   This file contains SLR-derived C20 using TSVD and TSVD MM (see reference).
   TSVD MM is the recommended solution.
   Each estimate is based on 28 or 56 days of laser ranging from up to 3 MEO SLR satellites.
   The MEO SLR satellites are LAGEOS-1 (1976 Launch), LAGEOS-2 (1992), and LARES-2 (2022).
   The epoch of each estimate is the mid-point of the span used.
Citation:
   Loomis et al., 2025, Geophys. Res. Lett., https://doi.org/10.1029/2024GL114472
Notes:
   AOD1B RL06 model applied for de-aliasing.
   Add the AOD1B 28-day mean to the estimates to form the total C20 signal.
   C20 is zero tide.
   Sigmas were calibrated with C20 differences to Technical Note 14.
Format: (F7.4,E18.10,2F13.4,E18.10,3F13.4) 
   Column  1: Year and fraction of year of solution mid-point
   Column  2: TSVD C20
   Column  3: TSVD C20 - mean C20 (1.0E-10)
   Column  4: TSVD C20 Sigma (1.0E-10)
   Column  5: TSVD MM C20
   Column  6: TSVD MM C20 - mean C20 (1.0E-10)
   Column  7: TSVD MM C20 Sigma (1.0E-10)
   Column  8: AOD1B 28-day mean (1.0E-10)
Constants:
   Mean C20: -4.841694086827E-04
         GM: 0.3986004415E+06 (km^3/s^2)
          R: 6378.1363 (km)
